records.detail: Bank Al-Maghrib Rapport Annuel 2025, accounting-principles note 'Les autres avoirs en devises' (same note in the 2024 English edition is on p.226): the Bank holds portfolios of US dollar securities whose management is delegated to the World Bank under delegation contracts, and the securities are revalued from the net asset values communicated by the managing agent ('mandataire de gestion'). The profit-and-loss table 'Autres produits financiers' shows capital gains on management mandates (plus-values des mandats de gestion) of 452,544 thousand dirhams in 2025 against 202,309 thousand in 2024 and 353,114 thousand in 2023. 'Mandats de gestion' is also a line of the foreign-currency holdings table, included in the 'Others' row of holdings and placements in foreign currencies (16,386,426 thousand dirhams, 5% of the total 339,309,229 thousand at 31 December 2024). The report does not say which World Bank unit runs the mandates, so the entity is keyed to World Bank Treasury. English wording, 2024 edition: 'The Bank holds portfolios of securities denominated in US dollars, whose management is delegated to the World Bank by virtue of delegation contracts' (https://www.bkam.ma/en/content/download/829011/9037413/Rapport%2024%20ANG.pdf).
records.source_title: Bank Al-Maghrib, Rapport Annuel 2025 (note 'Les autres avoirs en devises'; tableau 'Autres produits financiers')

records.detail: National Bank of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Annual Report 2024, section on management of gold and foreign exchange assets: 'In order to expand investments in Chinese government securities, participation in the Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership program was approved by appointing the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development as an external manager for part of the assets of the emerging markets portfolio.' The same section's portfolio table puts the emerging markets portfolio at USD 233.1 million, 0.5% of gold and foreign exchange assets, at 1 January 2025 (USD 228.3 million, 0.6%, a year earlier), out of USD 45,648.3 million of total gold and FX assets. The report names the IBRD rather than RAMP as the manager, so the entity is keyed to World Bank Treasury. It does not state the size of the IBRD slice inside that portfolio or a start date.

records.detail: Korea Investment Corporation's Santiago Principles self-assessment published by the International Forum of Sovereign Wealth Funds (KIC, 2025). Under Principle 4 it says KIC manages assets 'entrusted by the government, the Bank of Korea and other public funds defined under the National Finance Act', and it cites Article 1 of the KIC Act for its purpose and Articles 2 and 30 of the KIC Act with Article 11 of the Enforcement Decree for funding and withdrawal. What the document does not say: it does not call the entrusted Bank of Korea assets foreign exchange reserves, gives no amount for the Bank of Korea portion, and gives no start date. KIC is a separate statutory corporation, not an internal unit of the Bank of Korea. Marked weak because the text is carried on the IFSWF site rather than on the Bank of Korea's or KIC's own site.
records.source_title: IFSWF, Santiago Principles Self-Assessment — Korea Investment Corporation (2025), Principles 2 and 4
records.quote: entrusted by the government, the Bank of Korea and other public funds

confirmed_blank.note: Banque de la République d'Haïti, audited annual financial statements for the year ended 30 September 2023 (auditors Firme Turnier and Ernst & Young (Racine)) — accounting-policies note 1(d) 'Placements en devises étrangères' and the financial-risk note that opens the liquidity-risk section. The policy note says the BRH chose a system of management by external portfolio administrators ('un système de gestion par administrateurs externes de portefeuille (gestion déléguée)') and that the portfolio managers may have discretionary powers or strict limits; the risk note puts the BRH investment portfolio held with the external managers at $1,807,431,480 at 30 September 2023, made up of cash, bonds, equities and the gold on deposit at the Banque de Montréal. No manager is named anywhere in the statements. The only firms named are Citibank New York (deposit and collateral accounts, note on Citibank collateral) and the Banque de Montréal (gold on deposit, note 4) — both custody or deposit rows, not management. Provenance note: the PDF was already present in the shared round-67 download directory (fetched by another agent this round); I read and grepped the text myself but did not fetch the URL.

Reserve Bank of Vanuatu audited financial statements 2019 (https://www.rbv.gov.vu/images/Annual_Financial_Statement/RBV_FS_2019_Final_Signed.pdf), Note 9 Operating Expenses and Note 25 on reserves management. Note 9 carries a 'Funds managers'' expense line of VT6,357 thousand for 2019 against VT6,069 thousand for 2018, so fees are paid to outside managers, but no firm is named and no managed balance is given. Note 25 describes the reserves as run under the Bank's own investment guidelines and risk processes with no outside manager. The Annual Report 2022 (https://rbv.gov.vu/images/Annual_Reports/Annual%20Report%202022.pdf) names none either, giving only official reserves of VT70,966.9 million at September 2022; the 'Official Foreign Reserves & Exchange Rate Management' section at pp.24-26 was past the first 100,000 characters I could read, so that section is unread.

Bank of Finland, Annual Report on Responsible Investment 2024 (https://www.suomenpankki.fi/globalassets/bof/en/bank-of-finland/climate-measures/responsible-investment/bank-of-finland-annual-report-on-responsible-investment-2024.pdf), the opening section on the Bank's financial assets and Table 1. It states that 'Some of the financial assets are also invested in equity, real estate and fixed-income funds through external asset managers', and later sections describe selecting and monitoring fund managers, sending them an annual ESG survey, and holding asset-manager meetings — so external managers plainly run part of the portfolio. No manager is named anywhere in the report, and no amount is attached to the externally managed share; Table 1 breaks the assets down only by gold (EUR 3,532 million) and foreign reserves (EUR 8,427 million) at 31 December 2024.

Nepal Rastra Bank, Financial Statements FY 2081/82 (https://www.nrb.org.np/contents/uploads/2025/11/Financial-Statements-81.82-for-upload.pdf), full set. A grep of the whole document for 'externally managed', 'fund manager', 'asset manager', 'investment manager', 'portfolio manager' and 'RAMP' returns nothing; the only 'mandate' hits are NRB directives mandating bank lending. No outside manager of the reserves is named or implied.

Central Bank of The Gambia Annual Report and Financial Statements for 2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022, plus the separate Annual Reports for 2020, 2022 and 2023 (all from cbg.gm/downloads-file/). Crown Agents appears, but only as a banker: it is in the 'Bankers' list on the directors'/corporate-information page alongside the Bank of England, the IMF, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Banque de France, the BIS, Standard Chartered, UBAF, Deutsche Bundesbank and Banco Santander, and in the credit-quality tables for 'Fixed term investment USD - Current' and '- Non Current' with carrying amount, maximum exposure, denomination, collateral and credit-rating columns. Those are counterparty and deposit rows, not a management mandate, so under the no-upgrade rule nothing is filed. No 'external manager', 'fund manager' or RAMP mention appears in any of the eleven documents.

Banque Centrale de Tunisie, Rapport Annuel 2025 (published July 2026) and Rapport Annuel 2024, full French texts. Greps for 'gestion déléguée', 'mandats de gestion', 'gestionnaire externe', 'délégation', 'Banque mondiale' and 'BRI' return only the abbreviation list and macroeconomic citations of World Bank commodity-price data and BIS material; nothing on anyone managing the BCT's reserves. Caveat: the copies I could read are mirrors on leaders.com.tn and chaexpert.com, because bct.gov.tn's document index returned 404 and I could not find the official PDF path.

Banque Centrale des Comores, Rapport annuel 2024 (https://banque-comores.km/uploads/Rapport-annuel-BCC-2024.pdf), the foreign-reserves and placements passages and the balance-sheet commentary. Greps for 'gestionnaire', 'gestion déléguée', 'administrateur externe' and 'Banque mondiale' find only a museum manager, World Bank project financing and World Bank debt — no outside manager of the reserves. The report describes the reserves and placements without naming any manager.

Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Annual Report 2025 (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/Annual%20report_2025.pdf), section 2.4 on foreign exchange reserve management: 'In managing foreign exchange reserves, the Central Bank continued to cooperate with external managers alongside internal management.' So external managers are used, but none is named; income from managing FX assets was $505.5 million, a 4.6% return, and official FX reserves rose $555.4 million (5.1%) to $11.5 billion. The Annual Report 2023 (https://uploads.cbar.az/assets/Annual%20report%20final%202023.pdf) likewise reports AZN5.0 million of accounting losses on derivative financial instruments 'managed by an external manager' without naming it.

Danmarks Nationalbank Årsrapport 2025 (88 pages, editorial close 17 February 2026) — greps of the whole Danish text for 'ekstern'/'forvalt'/'mandat'/'manager' return only the Nationalbank's own mandate and its role as state debt manager (statsgældsforvalter). Separately, the Central Banking 'Reserve manager' award citation for the National Bank of Denmark (https://www.centralbanking.com/awards/7960610/reserve-manager-national-bank-of-denmark) names Eurex, Eurex Clearing and Clearstream Banking, but as the CCP platform, clearing house and collateral/settlement provider it joined (talks from May 2022, decision February 2023, live in August) — market infrastructure, not reserve management — and the ECB only as the setter of deposit remuneration. Nothing to file. Provenance note: the Årsrapport PDF was already in the shared round-67 download directory; I read and grepped the text but did not fetch the URL.

Central Bank of Cyprus Annual Report (122 pages, Eurosystem branding, PDF created 15 May 2026, so the 2025 report) — greps for 'managed by', 'external manage', 'mandate' and 'custodian' return only the Bank's institutional mandate, team mandates, the Investor Compensation Fund managed by a Management Committee, and a reference to 'lending programmes operated by international custodians' for its bonds. A securities-lending programme run by a custodian is a custody arrangement, not a management mandate, so nothing is filed. Provenance note: PDF already present in the shared round-67 download directory; text read and grepped by me, URL not fetched.

Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino, 'Relazione consuntiva sull'attività svolta e sull'andamento del sistema finanziario — Anno 2025' (95 pages). Every 'gestione'/'depositaria'/'mandati' hit is about the San Marino financial system it supervises — società di gestione, the depositary-bank business of local intermediaries (EUR 423 million, up EUR 85 million), gestioni di patrimoni mobiliari, and fiduciary-administration mandates of types 2 and 4 — not about anyone managing the central bank's own assets. Nothing to file. Provenance note: PDF already present in the shared round-67 download directory; text read and grepped by me, URL not fetched.

Monetary Authority of Macao Annual Report (83 pages, data to end-2022). The reserves passage says only 'Exchange reserves and other foreign assets managed by the AMCM shrank year-on-year by 1.8% to MOP219.6 billion at end-2022' — managed by the AMCM itself. The report's 'outsourcing' references are its own Guideline on Outsourcing for supervised banks and insurers, and 'custodians' appears only as a category of entities in the local fund industry. No outside manager of the AMCM's reserves is named. Provenance note: PDF already present in the shared round-67 download directory; text read and grepped by me, URL not fetched, and this is the 2022 edition rather than the latest.

Central Bank of Sudan, 64th Annual Report 2024 (223 pages, Arabic). Greps for 'managed by', 'external manage', 'mandate', 'custodian', 'RAMP' and 'World Bank Treasury' return nothing at all in the extracted text. No outside manager of the reserves appears. Caveat: the text layer is Arabic and my patterns were Latin-script, so an Arabic-only phrase could have been missed; this one is worth a re-read with Arabic search terms. Provenance note: PDF already present in the shared round-67 download directory.

Banque Centrale de Djibouti annual reports for 2017 through 2024 (eight French PDFs). Greps across all eight for 'externe'/'gestionnaire'/'fund manager'/'asset manager'/'RAMP' return only FATF/GAFIMOAN recommendations and the Bank's own mandate; no outside manager of the reserves is named in any year. Provenance note: the PDFs were already present in the shared round-67 download directory; text read and grepped by me, URLs not fetched.

Banque Centrale du Congo annual report (202 pages, French, PDF created March 2026). Greps for 'gestionnaire', 'externally managed', 'fund manager', 'asset manager' and 'RAMP' return only the BCC's own 'agences mandataires' (its provincial agent branches) and, in a list of supervised insurance intermediaries, health-insurance managers ('gestionnaire assurance maladie'). Nothing about anyone managing the BCC's reserves. Provenance note: PDF already present in the shared round-67 download directory.

needs_a_hand_check.why: Central Banking's 2025 'Reserve manager' award citation for Bank Indonesia (https://www.centralbanking.com/awards/7972253/reserve-manager-bank-indonesia, published March 2025) says the bank does sustainable investing by 'investing in thematic funds such as BISIP G3', described in the article as the Bank for International Settlements' Asia green bond fund, and separately that the bank 'use[s] benchmarks for external managers'. For: the BIS manages the BISIP pools, so an outside body runs money for Bank Indonesia. Against: this is a holding of units in a pooled fund rather than a mandate given to a manager, which is close to the counterparty/holding exclusion, the citation gives no amount and no start date, the external managers themselves are not named, and the source is trade press behind a partial paywall (weak_source would be true). Not filed as a record; the owner should decide whether a BIS investment pool counts on this row.

Banka Slovenije Annual Report 2025 (https://www.bsi.si/storage/uploads/3a54bc7a-9890-411f-8afa-d57032671230/Annual-Report-2025.pdf), financial-assets section and the balance-sheet note on investment funds. The maturity breakdown says the longest bucket includes 'holdings in a BIS fund and of equity ETFs, which have no maturity'; equity ETFs are 9% of the portfolio; the note line 'Investment funds' is EUR 665,430 thousand against EUR 599,486 thousand a year earlier, and the earlier text says the Bank invests a portion of its financial assets in exchange-traded funds. For: the BIS fund and the ETFs are run by outside bodies. Against: these are fund unit holdings, not mandates, the BIS fund is not separately quantified or even named beyond 'a BIS fund', the ETF providers are not named, and the report says the asset management process is run by the Bank's own Investment Committee. Not filed; same question as Indonesia.

Central Banking's 2026 'Reserve manager' award citation for the Central Bank of the Philippines (https://www.centralbanking.com/awards/7975043/reserve-manager-central-bank-of-the-philippines, 10 March 2026) opens by listing updated 'external fund manager rules' among the year's reserve-management changes, so the BSP does use external fund managers, but the article text cuts off mid-sentence at the paywall and names none. The BSP's own site (www.bsp.gov.ph) returns 403 to this session, so the audited financial statements could not be read. Recorded as paywalled plus blocked rather than blank: the BSP statements have not actually been tested on this row.

Central Banking benchmarking pieces 'Reserve managers name top bank counterparties and asset managers' (node/7973748), 'Asset delegation to external managers averages just 12%' (node/7962282), 'Large reserve holders use external managers for intel and new assets' (node/7962310) and 'Securities lending banks engage external managers for new assets' (7973701) — survey write-ups that may name asset managers but, being survey aggregates, are unlikely to tie a named manager to a named central bank; not opened.

Bank of Finland Financial Statements 2020-2023 on publications.bof.fi were not opened; they may quantify or name the external asset managers that the 2024 responsible-investment report says run the equity, real estate and fixed-income fund holdings.
